gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-decorator-vs-chain:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-decorator-vs-chain:a: an independent reader (37-structural-patterns q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-decorator-vs-chain:a: ruled out: That stop-at-first-handler behavior is attributed to Chain of Responsibility, not Decorator: "Chain of Responsibility: ... MAY stop at any handler" versus "Decorator ALWAYS delegates to the next wrapper."
recorded.prompt:q-decorator-vs-chain:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-decorator-vs-chain:c: an independent reader (37-structural-patterns q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-decorator-vs-chain:c: ruled out: Picking one layer per call describes Strategy, not Decorator: "Strategy: ... The client selects one strategy at a time... Strategies are alternatives, not cumulative."
recorded.prompt:q-decorated-identity:b: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-decorated-identity:b: an independent reader (37-structural-patterns q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-decorated-identity:b: ruled out: The page gives this exact example and states directly: "Notifier original = new EmailNotifier(...); Notifier decorated = new SmsDecorator(original, ...); // original == decorated is FALSE". Forwarding calls does not make decorated the same object.
recorded.prompt:q-decorated-identity:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-decorated-identity:c: an independent reader (37-structural-patterns q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-decorated-identity:c: ruled out: The page separates == from equals(): "// original == decorated is FALSE" is stated unconditionally, while "original.equals(decorated) depends on equals() implementation" is the only thing tied to an equals() override. Overriding equals() does not change what == compares in Java.
